keyword: save for a wedding, Hajj or Umrah

seo.title: Saving for a Wedding, Hajj or Umrah: A Monthly Plan
seo.description: Set a target, work out the monthly amount, use a sinking fund and choose where to keep the money while saving for a wedding, Hajj or Umrah in Pakistan.

h1: How to save for a wedding, Hajj or Umrah
summary: How to set a target for a wedding, Hajj or Umrah, work out what to save each month, keep the money safe while it grows, and bring the total cost down, with worked examples in rupees.
intro_html:
A wedding, Hajj or Umrah is one of the biggest costs most families in Pakistan ever plan for. Too often, the money comes from a loan, a rushed committee or selling gold at the last minute.

A steady plan works better. Choose a target, divide it into monthly amounts, keep the money somewhere safe that earns a little profit, and look for ways to bring the total down. This guide shows how, step by step.

sections.body_html:
How much to save each month to reach three example targets:

GoalTargetTimeMonthly, no profitMonthly, with profit (our calculation)
Hajj (government scheme, 40-day package for 2027)Rs 12,00,00024 monthsRs 50,000about Rs 45,700
Umrah (example)Rs 4,00,00018 monthsRs 22,200about Rs 20,800
Wedding (example)Rs 15,00,00024 monthsRs 62,500about Rs 57,200

The Hajj figure is the government scheme price for 2027 reported by Business Recorder in August 2026. The Umrah and wedding targets are examples only, because costs vary widely with the package, the season and the family. "With profit" assumes 10% a year with 15% tax withheld, about 8.5% after tax, with profit added monthly. That is our calculation based on the National Savings Account rate in October 2026, not a promise of future returns.

Hajj

The Ministry of Religious Affairs sets the price of the government Hajj scheme each year. For Hajj 2027, Business Recorder reported in August 2026 a price of Rs 1.2 million for the 40-day package and Rs 1.3 million for the 20 to 25-day package. Applicants paid 50% with the application from 17 August 2026, and Express Tribune reported a second-instalment deadline of 5 to 20 October 2026; missing it cancels the application.

So if you plan for a future year, have most of the money ready by the summer before Hajj, not by Hajj itself. Private packages cost more and vary by operator.

Umrah

Umrah has no official price. Add up the visa, return flights, hotels in Makkah and Madinah, transport and food. Fares are usually higher in Ramazan and school holidays, so get two or three quotes for the dates you want.

Wedding

List every event and cost: venue, food, clothes, jewellery, gifts, photography, transport and the cost of hosting relatives. Agree the total as a family before anyone books anything.

Allow for rising prices

Prices rose 9.6% in the year to October 2026, according to the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics. If a Rs 12 lakh cost rose 7.05% a year (the 2025-26 average), it would be about Rs 13.75 lakh in two years (our calculation). Add a margin of 10% to 15% to any goal more than a year away.

sections.h2: Step 2: work out the monthly amount
sections.body_html:
The basic sum is simple: target ÷ months left = monthly saving.

For example, Rs 4,00,000 for Umrah in 18 months is about Rs 22,200 a month. If that is too much, you have three choices: save for longer, lower the target, or find extra income. Write the number down and treat it like a bill you pay on payday.

Not sure what you can afford? Our monthly budget plan for any salary in Pakistan shows what a realistic savings line looks like at different incomes.

A sinking fund is money set aside each month for one known cost. Keep each goal in its own account or clearly labelled pot, so wedding money isn't spent on a fridge repair.

  • One goal, one pot. A separate savings account, certificate or wallet for each big goal.
  • Automate it. Ask your bank for a standing instruction to move the amount on payday.
  • Keep your emergency fund separate. If a medical bill comes, it shouldn't wipe out the Hajj fund. See our emergency fund guide.
  • Add windfalls. Put part of every bonus, Eidi or increment into the fund.

sections.h2: Step 4: decide where to keep the money
sections.body_html:
For a goal one to three years away, safety and easy access matter more than high returns. The common options:

  • A bank savings account. Under State Bank of Pakistan rules, the minimum profit for individuals is linked to the SBP repo rate. Deposits are protected up to Rs 10 lakh per depositor per bank by the Deposit Protection Corporation.
  • National Savings. From 21 October 2026, Dawn reported 10% on the Savings Account, 11.12% on 3-month Short Term Savings Certificates and 11.84% on the Sarwa Islamic Savings Account. Filers pay 15% tax on profit, non-filers 30%.
  • A committee. No profit, but an early turn can bring the money forward. Read the risks in our guide to committees, bank savings and National Savings.
  • Gold. Many families save in gold. Its price can fall as well as rise, and buying and selling has costs, so it suits money you won't need on a fixed date.

Zakat: banks deduct zakat on 1 Ramazan from savings accounts at or above the nisab, which was set at Rs 5,03,529 for the zakat year 1446-47 (2026). Savings for Hajj or a wedding still count. Ask a scholar how zakat applies to you.

sections.h2: Step 5: bring the total cost down
sections.body_html:
Wedding

  • Agree a guest list and a budget before booking the hall, and stick to both.
  • Combine events, such as mehndi and mayun, or hold one at home.
  • Choose a weekday or an off-season date, when halls may offer a lower price.
  • Rent or reuse outfits, and buy jewellery by weight rather than heavy designs that carry high making charges.

Hajj and Umrah

  • Apply for the government scheme early and follow the Ministry's dates exactly.
  • For Umrah, compare packages for the same dates and check what each includes: hotel distance from the Haram, meals and transport.
  • Travel outside Ramazan and school holidays if you can.
  • Pay only registered operators and keep every receipt.

faq.q: How much does Hajj cost from Pakistan in 2027?
faq.a: Business Recorder reported in August 2026 that the government scheme for Hajj 2027 costs Rs 1.2 million for the 40-day package and Rs 1.3 million for the 20 to 25-day package. Private packages cost more. Check the Ministry of Religious Affairs for the final figures.

faq.q: How much should I save each month for Hajj?
faq.a: Divide the package price by the months you have. Rs 1.2 million over 24 months is Rs 50,000 a month, or about Rs 45,700 if the money earns about 8.5% a year after tax (our calculation). Remember that half is paid with the application.

faq.q: Where should I keep money for a wedding or Hajj?
faq.a: Somewhere safe that you can reach on time: a separate bank savings account or a National Savings account or certificate. A committee can bring the money forward but earns no profit and depends on every member paying.

faq.q: How can I reduce wedding costs in Pakistan?
faq.a: Agree the guest list and total budget first, combine events, choose an off-season or weekday date, rent or reuse outfits, and save for the wedding in a separate pot so the cost doesn't end up on loans or credit cards.

faq.q: Is zakat deducted from my Hajj savings?
faq.a: Banks deduct zakat on 1 Ramazan from savings accounts with a balance at or above the nisab, set at Rs 503,529 for the zakat year 1446-47. Savings for Hajj are usually counted. Ask a scholar about your situation.
